simple.meaning: אַשְׁקְלוֹן (ʼAshqᵉlôwn) appears 12 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with kingship. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering.

definitions.full: H831. Ashqelon אַשְׁקְלוֺן proper name, of a location a city of the Philistines (Assyrian Isqaluna COT Gloss Dl Pa 290 ; Phoenician adjective, of a people compare below) Judg 1:18 ; 14:19 ; 1Sam 6:17 ; 2Sam 1:20 ; Jer 25:20 ; 47:5 , 7 ; Amos 1:8 ; Zeph 2:4 , 7 ; Zech 9:5 (twice in verse); on the Mediterranean Sea, south of west from Jerusalem, modern `Asqalân , Survey iii. 237 f. (with plan); compare also ZPV ii. 164 f .
definitions.rootNote: probably from 8254 in the sense of weighing-place (i.e. mart);

occurrences.englishText: Also Judah took Gaza with its border, and Ashkelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.

Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck thirty men of them. He took their plunder, then gave the changes of clothing to those who declared the riddle. His anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.
These are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering to Yahweh: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;
and all the mixed people, and all the kings of the land of Uz, all the kings of the Philistines, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod,
For Gaza will be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation. They will drive out Ashdod at noonday, and Ekron will be rooted up.

The coast will be for the remnant of the house of Judah. They will find pasture. In the houses of Ashkelon, they will lie down in the evening, for Yahweh, their God, will visit them, and restore them.
Ashkelon will see it, and fear;
